Yes. The subtext enriches the story naturally rather than feeling forced. Ilse’s gift of the bicycle light, despite knowing it will not be returned, reveals care beneath her terse manner. Her silence when the visitor asks whether the ferry is worthwhile suggests a value in her work that passenger numbers cannot capture.

Most poignantly, her unanswered call from Jonas—possibly the son mentioned earlier—hints at emotional distance without explaining its cause. Against her dependable service to others, that refusal introduces a private vulnerability. The fog, disappearing shores, and connecting cable deepen these themes of connection and isolation while remaining convincing details of the ferry’s setting.
